messages:
alyssa: Heads up — ran into a weird combo when using the Python SDK against a Dedicated endpoint behind our proxy/VPC. Sync client works with custom CA but async client fails TLS.
ben: Can you paste the minimal repro? async vs sync libs matter (httpx vs requests etc).
alyssa: Yep. Using httpx.AsyncClient + sdk.AsyncClient(base_url=\"https://redwood-internal.local\", api_key=os.getenv('REDWOOD_API_KEY')) and I pass `verify='/etc/ssl/custom-ca.pem'` to AsyncClient. Sync (requests) with same CA file -> OK. Async -> cert verify error:
alyssa: ```
ssl.SSLCertVerificationError: [SSL: CERTIFICATE_VERIFY_FAILED] certificate verify failed: unable to get local issuer certificate (_ssl.c:xxx)
```
ciara: Did you pass the CA to the SDK or to httpx explicitly? Our SDK accepts `base_url` and `verify` but the async path historically forwarded to httpx differently.
alyssa: I tried both: `Client(verify='/etc/ssl/custom-ca.pem')` and creating `httpx.AsyncClient(verify='/etc/ssl/custom-ca.pem')` and passing that in `sdk.AsyncClient(transport=...)` — still fails.
ben: Also check env var `REQUESTS_CA_BUNDLE` vs `SSL_CERT_FILE` vs `HTTPX_CLIENT_TLS` — we don't have a standardized env name. Strange that requests honors it and httpx doesn't by default.
ciara: Async httpx uses ssl.SSLContext if you pass a path it should create context. Maybe our type hints caused overloads to coerce the param away? @alyssa can you run a tiny script that prints the type of `client._transport._pool._ssl_context` (or whatever httpx stores) after init?
alyssa: Quick dump shows None on async client, and valid SSLContext on sync.
alyssa: Minimal script attached: ```
import httpx
c = httpx.AsyncClient(verify='/etc/ssl/custom-ca.pem')
print(getattr(c, 'verify', None))
``` -> prints the path string, but runtime path->SSLContext conversion seems to be skipped when used through our SDK.
ciara: OK that smells like an SDK wrapper bug. We convert kwargs for AsyncClient differently to inject our retry/auth middleware.
ben: Also noticed typing mismatch in AsyncClient constructor in our stub: `verify: Optional[bool]` (wrong) vs httpx allowing Union[bool, str, ssl.SSLContext]. If our signature is too narrow, mypy users might pass the path and the wrapper could coerce it.
alyssa: That aligns — mypy forced me to wrap as bool earlier in other code. I didn't do that here but maybe runtime wrapper coalesces.
infra-bot: New issue created: #INF-4123 "py-sdk async client: custom CA path not applied to SSLContext via proxy/VPC" (assigned ciara)
ciara: I'll take it. Plan: add an explicit ssl.SSLContext creation when verify is str/path and ensure the async transport gets it. Also fix typing to `Union[bool, str, ssl.SSLContext]` in stubs.
ben: Can you add a small regression test that simulates our internal proxy by using a local cert and http.server + ssl? Keep it unit-level, no network flakiness.
ciara: Yep. Also need to check retries: current retry middleware rewraps the request and may be recreating transport without the ssl context during a retry on connection error — will audit.
alyssa: For now workaround I used: create ssl context manually and pass as `verify=ssl_context` into httpx.AsyncClient, then pass that client into sdk.AsyncClient(httpx_client=async_client). That worked.
ben: Thanks for the workaround — can you paste that snippet in the issue to help reproducer? Also mention Dedicated vs Hosted because hosted uses public certs so not affected.
alyssa: Done.
ciara: I'll push a PR to fix constructor forwarding + typing + test. Hoping for patch release this week.
alyssa: 🙏 One more ask: can we add a short note in the Python SDK quickstart about environment vars and using custom CAs for Dedicated/Private? Saved me 2 hrs.
ben: Agreed — adding a small doc blurb and example with both sync and async patterns.
infra-bot: PR opened: https://git.redwood/internal/sdk-python/pulls/829 (ci checks queued)
alyssa: Thanks folks! I'll retest once the patch lands.
